title: Indonesia Needs to Do More to Tackle the Region’s Transboundary Haze Problem
author: Edmund Lim
text:
Air pollution in North Kayong regency, West Kalimantan province, Indonesia, Sep. 27, 2026.
Credit: Wikimedia Commons/OttaEl
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto is the key leader in ASEAN who can and should do better in haze management in the coming years. The current haze situation affecting Southeast Asia is, to a certain extent, a reflection of his leadership and management, given that most of it stems from fires happening in his country.Forests and peatlands in Indonesia have been burning substantially this year and millions of people in Southeast Asia are suffering as a result. In early September, Kuching had the worst air quality of any large city on earth. Malaysian authorities declared a state of emergency in the Serian district of Sarawak, as the Air Pollutant Index exceeded 500. The Philippines closed schools throughout Metro Manila and more than 12 provinces. The regional haze monitor in ASEAN reached level three, the most severe on the scale.[...]
